newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Israeli troops wound seven Palestinians in Hebron.
newsitem.headline: Israeli troops wound seven Palestinians in Hebron.

text.p: Israeli soldiers shot and wounded seven Palestinians on Thursday in clashes with Arab stone-throwers in the West Bank, witnesses and hospital officials said.

Palestinians in Hebron, a flashpoint of Jewish-Arab violence, said young demonstrators wielding sling shots fought Israeli soldiers across an invisible line that divides Hebron into Israeli- and Palestinian-controlled areas. Some youths hurled petrol bombs.
Soldiers in riot gear fought back with rubber-coated metal bullets wounding at least seven demonstrators, witnesses and hospital officials said.
Palestinian police, who managed to control the stone- throwers in the beginning, appeared helpless as the clashes spread to other parts of town.
An Israeli army spokeswoman said three petrol bombs were thrown at troops. She knew of no Palestinian casualties.

Clashes also erupted briefly in Bethlehem, where scores of Palestinian university students marched towards Israeli army lines and hurled stones. Troops fired tear gas and rubber bullets but there were no reports of casualties.

Israel's groundbreaking on a Jewish settlement in Arab East Jerusalem on March 18 has sparked almost daily Palestinian protests and clashes with Israeli security forces. Israeli settlers and troops killed three Palestinians in Hebron on Tuesday.
Earlier on Thursday, Israel's defence minister warned his troops could easily reoccupy cities Israel handed over to the PLO under self-rule deals but preferred not to do so.

"There would be no difficulty recapturing Hebron or any other city but we don't want to do that," Yithzak Mordechai told soldiers in northern Israel. "We want the Palestinians to honour the agreements."
"We wish Mr Mordechai would stop issuing such empty threats. Entering (Palestinian cities) would not be easy," said Ahmed Abdel-Rahman, secretary-general of the Palestinian Authority.
Palestinians said the Israeli army imposed a curfew on the West Bank village of Surif and detained five Palestinians, including the director of a private hospital in Hebron.
